title: Every scaffolded artifact carries a generated-header citing blueprint_id + version + sha256
statement: Every file emitted by a SKILL-scaffold-* skill MUST contain a generated-header citing the producing blueprint's id, version, and the 8-character head of the canonical-JSON sha256 of the blueprint at scaffold time. The header is the forensic anchor: drift between the artifact's declared blueprint_version and the on-disk blueprint's current version (or between declared sha256 head and recomputed sha256 head) is a hard-fail at audit time. The scaffold-evidence record (scaffold-evidence.schema.json) is the registry; per-file headers are the inline witnesses.
rationale: Per D-59. Scaffolders emit large diffs into adopter code, and adopters frequently edit scaffolded files thereafter. The header is intentionally NOT a freeze: manual edits to scaffolded code are explicitly allowed (the substrate is a starting point, not a frozen artifact). What the header does is record provenance: any future maintainer can answer 'which blueprint version emitted this file?' by reading the header, and the audit can detect 'scaffolded file diverged from blueprint without a regeneration cycle.' Severity gate: observational at edit time, blocking only at audit/release time when drift exceeds a configurable threshold (Phase 18.F sets the threshold per skill).

strategy.rationale: The registered test corpus provides deterministic regression evidence for this invariant.
